objective: 0.3.0 pi 11/12: Make T3 Code the primary interface for HolyAgent on pi and integrate deeply with it: T3 runs pi through `pi --mode rpc`, HolyAgent uses T3's own dialogs, browser and visual tools, enables T3's beneficial settings, adds computer use through Cua Driver, and keeps only the T3 tools it needs.
requirements: Maintainer (verbatim): "also I want holyagent pi to be compatible with t3 code"; scope "In 0.3.0"; then "t3code shall be the primary interface for the pi integration, so we will deeply integrate with it. that means we can rely on its integrated browser, computer use, as well as enable anything beneficial we can from it globally or locally". The maintainer implements 0.3.0; this Intent records the plan.

Maintainer, 2026-11-07: implement 0.3.0 now, every part except the dropped auto-mode gate (pi 8/10); test with unit tests and recorded or synthesized fixtures only, no live Kimi runs; merge each PR once it is reviewed and green.

Facts (research assignment-0mw6r54ng-kg9r, sources pingdotgg/t3code docs/user/providers-pi.md and PR #7211): T3 Code runs the user's own pi install as a built-in provider (Early Access, pi 0.80.5 or newer, enabled in T3 Settings) through `pi --mode rpc` over stdio JSONL, rejects launch args that change mode or session, carries pi's models, auth, extensions, skills and context files, and injects its own MCP bridge extension (prefix mcp__t3-code__).
HolyAgent pi works in rpc mode (ctx.mode "rpc", hasUI true) and sets no launch args for mode or session.

Decided (maintainer: "I want tthem to run with t3code's dialogs/ui, no weird tui stuff"): under T3, every HolyAgent interaction uses only the RPC extension UI that T3 renders (select, confirm, input, editor in T3's composer; notify to the work log; setStatus near the composer) and never custom(), widgets, footer, titles or theme calls; the ask-user and todo tools (rpiv) follow this, with a HolyAgent adapter where a package relies on custom() TUI rendering.

Decided (maintainer: "Require Full access"): HolyAgent threads in T3 run in T3's Full access mode, consistent with the full-access default; the docs and the setup check say so, and HolyAgent warns when a T3 session runs in Supervised or Auto-accept edits, where every extension tool call prompts and background specialists could stall.

Decided (maintainer: "pi's stuff"): specialists report back through @tintinweb/pi-subagents' own new-turn trigger, not T3's delegate_task; a recorded fixture of T3's RPC traffic verifies that a completion notice arriving after agent_settled starts a new root turn in T3.

Decided (maintainer: "t3code can delegate stuff with their mcp, can we disable whatever is unnecessary from it?"; research assignment-0mw6r9zxs-l85j): HolyAgent keeps T3's html_render, html_preview, preview_*, t3_preview_* and device_* tools (its visual route and device access) and deactivates T3's orchestration tools (orchestrator_capabilities, delegate_task, task_status, task_cancel, create_threads, t3_thread_*, schedule_task, list_scheduled_tasks, delete_scheduled_task, t3_pending_request and any other mcp__t3-code__ tool outside those families) with pi.setActiveTools filtered by prefix from getAllTools(), applied once at session_start before the first request and reapplied on before_agent_start and session_tree, with a tool_call block as backstop; there is no T3 setting for this.

Prompt caching: the active tool set is fixed at session_start and not toggled mid-session, so the cached prefix holds (pi docs: setActiveTools changes provider tools; models without mid-conversation system messages take a cache miss per change).

To verify during implementation: the T3 release containing PR #7211; the exact preview_* set; whether T3's bridge re-adds tools after HolyAgent filters them; whether deferred tools stay discoverable through tool_search once excluded; pi 1.5.0 against T3's agent_settled and clear_queue assumptions; whether the rpiv packages use custom().
Tests: CI covers T3 with recorded fixtures of `pi --mode rpc` traffic inside the existing CI jobs, as the other pi tests do.

T3 Code is the primary interface for HolyAgent on pi: the docs lead with T3 Code, the plain pi terminal stays supported (maintainer: "Keep it supported"), with T3-only features falling back or reported unavailable there and CI covering both the terminal and T3's rpc mode, and HolyAgent relies on T3 features rather than rebuilding them (research assignment-0mw6rgzog-2rb3).

Browser: the visual roles use T3's integrated browser (preview_status, preview_open, preview_dialog, preview_navigate, preview_resize, preview_set_appearance, preview_snapshot, preview_act, preview_evaluate, preview_wait_for, preview_recording_start, preview_recording_stop) and html_render and html_preview; the fixed tool set pins these names, since on pi 0.99 and newer they are deferred behind tool_search.

Computer use (maintainer: "cua driver"; research assignment-0mw6rlor5-3o9f): T3 provides none for pi, so HolyAgent adds Cua Driver (trycua/cua, MIT; macOS 14+, Windows 10/11, Linux X11 or XWayland preview) through the existing pi extension @amaster.ai/pi-computer-use, pinned and moved by deps:update; it runs in standard permission mode with the extension's confirmations off (maintainer: "Full access, no prompts"), and only Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual get its tools; the driver is the copy the extension bundles (no separate install; the bundled version moves with the extension pin), and setup walks through the macOS Accessibility and Screen Recording permissions.

T3 device access (simulators, device_* tools) is enabled where the host supports it (macOS with Xcode, or the Android SDK); whether pi reaches device_* is verified during implementation (root default from "enable anything beneficial").

T3 settings (maintainer: "Setup writes them"): once the implementation verifies the format of T3's settings.json under T3CODE_HOME (default ~/.t3), holyagent setup for pi writes the beneficial T3 settings (pi provider enabled, worktrees, context meter, device access) globally or as per-project overrides, with an undo; when settings.json does not decode or the read-back differs, setup stops with an error naming the file and leaves it unchanged.

Relied on as they are: T3's model and effort pickers, checkpoints and rollback (pi session files), skills menu, worktrees, terminal, diff and PR flow; T3's scheduled tasks stay usable from T3's UI while their agent tools stay deactivated.

Maintainer (verbatim): "the context meter is the little context indicator? don't set it." Setup does not write T3's context meter, and the config has no key for it; the rest of the T3 settings setup writes are chosen by the maintainer from a full list of T3 settings.

T3 settings facts (research assignment-0mw6wtdf9-cxr4, /home/user/holyagent-notes/t3-settings.md): server settings live in ~/.t3/userdata/settings.json (Effect Schema in pingdotgg/t3code packages/contracts/src/settings.ts), watched by the server so external edits load, written sparsely with defaults stripped; a client save within about 100 ms can overwrite an external edit (issue #18571), so setup merges, writes atomically and reads back. Client settings (notifications, follow-up behavior, display) are per device and not in settings.json, so setup leaves them alone and prints nothing about them.

Maintainer (verbatim): "setup should be a tui with flags to set stuff, the options I check should be options, but the default isn't determined". The T3 part of holyagent setup for pi is a TUI with flags for each choice; it offers: enable the Pi provider (providerInstances.pi), agent device access (enableDeviceSupport and enableAgentDeviceAccess, only where Xcode or the Android SDK is present), and new threads in worktrees (defaultThreadEnvMode). Pi as the default model is not offered. defaultRuntimeMode full-access and enableAgentBrowserAccess true are restored only when they differ from T3's defaults.

Decided (maintainer): setup sets backgroundActivity overrides pauseWhenHostLocked, pauseWhenHostLowPower, pauseWhenClientLowPower and pauseWhenOnBattery to false, keeping the balanced profile otherwise, so unattended specialists never pause.

Decided (maintainer): setup sets sourceControlWritingStyle to Conventional Commits with no agent attribution (custom instructions) and removeAgentCreditsOnMerge true, so T3-made commits match HolyAgent's rules.

Maintainer (verbatim): "sorry, pi provider enabled shouldn't be optional when the pi.enable key in the holyagent config is true (true is the default). the other two should be selected by default. also the tui must use opentui solid, tuiparts and grab the exact same style from the last released holycodex tui". The config gains pi.enable (default true); while it is true setup always enables T3's Pi provider. In the TUI, agent device access and new threads in worktrees start selected. The setup TUI is built with OpenTUI Solid and copies the exact style of the last released holycodex TUI (v0.16.12, whose style equals v0.16.9-2's; maintainer: "0.16.9-2 wasnt the last release").

Maintainer (verbatim) "these should be enabled by default, without opting out. unless the user changes the t3 settings manually. these are just the defaults": setup always applies continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate on, autoResumeLimitedThreads on, worktree cleanup on merge, and newWorktreesStartFromOrigin on, with no TUI option, but writes a key only when the user has not set it in T3 (a value the user set by hand is left alone).
Maintainer (verbatim): "there are more relevant settings you are not asking me": more T3 settings are put to the maintainer before the setup TUI is built.

Maintainer (verbatim, on T3 git and PR settings): "mergeability first, figure out a way to do this that is always well mergeable", choosing branch naming rules, squash merges and auto-pull. Setup derives them per project from the target repository rather than fixing one value: branchNamingMode custom with branchNameInstructions that follow the repository's branch convention (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, branch history), pullRequestMergeMethod from the repository's allowed merge methods and convention (squash only where allowed and conventional), written as per-project overrides; defaultAutoPull on. Superseded in part (maintainer, 2026-11-09, choosing "Global rule only"; research assignment-0mw8tj2q7-d15a: T3 ProjectIds are random UUIDs minted when T3 adds a project, and t3.json carries only defaultThreadEnvMode and worktreeSubmodules): setup writes no per-project overrides; it writes the environment-wide branchNamingMode custom with branchNameInstructions telling T3 to follow each repository's own branch convention (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING, existing branches), only where unset; pullRequestMergeMethod stays at T3's default (null, the method last chosen on the device); setup reads no T3 database and runs no t3 project add.

Maintainer: setup also sets sidebarAutoSettleOnMerge on and snoozeLimitedThreads on; storageCleanup logsAfterDays, browserArtifactsAfterDays and worktreeSettledAfterDays are on as always-applied defaults (values chosen in implementation and documented), left alone when the user set them in T3.

Maintainer: T3 model choices (text generation, default thread model) stay manual; setup does not touch them. Pi launch settings (binaryPath, environment, update checks) stay at T3 defaults. Maintainer (verbatim): "if any of the settings we agreed is the default, don't set it at all": setup writes no key whose agreed value equals T3's default (defaultRuntimeMode full-access, enableAgentBrowserAccess, continueThreadsAfterServerUpdate, newWorktreesStartFromOrigin, sidebarAutoSettleOnMerge, followUpBehavior steer, planModeEnabled off); it still warns when a thread runs below Full access.

Maintainer (verbatim, 2026-11-07): "okay so leave out those printed steps": setup prints no per-device T3 steps (notifications, notification sound, follow-up behavior, plan mode, PR and chat links, browser viewport, appearance and recordings); per-device client settings stay as the user has them. The visual roles still resize with preview_resize to test responsiveness. Worktree submodules, worktree directory and the keep-uncommitted-changes cleanup rule stay at T3 defaults (root recommendation, maintainer: "whatever you recommend").

Decided (maintainer, choosing "No tuiparts"): @tuiparts/solid 0.0.6 requires OpenTUI 0.4.x and solid-js exactly 1.9.12, so the setup TUI uses no tuiparts; it uses current @opentui/solid (0.8.x) with its own elements (box, text, select, input) and builds checkboxes and rows in the holycodex style: Tokyo Night tokens from holycodex packages/cli/src/help.ts TERMINAL_THEME (heading #7aa2f7, option #7dcfff, argument #a9b1d6, focus #7dcfff bold, enabled #9ece6a, disabled #a9b1d6, success #73daca, warning #e0af68, error #f7768e, hint #737aa2), its colour policy (NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, FORCE_COLOR, CI, TTY), title 'HolyAgent  ·  setup', a key hint line, uppercase section headings, '❯ ' focus marker, '[x]'/'[ ]' checkboxes, a hint line for the focused row, and holycodex's keys (up/down or j/k, space toggles, Enter reviews, Esc or Ctrl-C cancels); tested headlessly with OpenTUI's test renderer (research assignment-0mw6zi93r-m1x2).

Decided (maintainer, 2026-11-08: "so don't include opencode browse"): HolyAgent does not add OpenCode browse (opencode.ai/product/browse, an MCP server and Chromium extension that drives the user's own browser); T3 Code's integrated browser stays the only agent browser, and the plain pi terminal keeps reporting the browser tools unavailable.

Found (research assignment-0mw8tj2q7-d15a): @juicesharp/rpiv-ask-user-question already uses only select and input under ctx.mode rpc, so it needs no adapter; @juicesharp/rpiv-todo works in RPC but its overlay is a component setWidget that Pi's RPC mode drops, so under T3 the todo list is visible only through tool results.
